name: Hiwassee/Ocoee Scenic River State Park - Gee Creek Campground
note: Gee Creek Campground: 47 drive-in sites on A and B loops, concrete pads 40-108 ft (some north-side Loop A sites need leveling). No hookups; potable water pumps, central bathhouse with hot showers, table/fire ring/grill per site. Seasonal (approx Apr 1-Oct 31), reservable online (reserve.tnstateparks.com). NOTE: park announced infrastructure renovation closing the campground fall 2026, reopening anticipated spring 2027. Operator: TN State Parks. --Claude  The reservation calendar now says the campground closes for renovation from early spring 2027 until summer 2028; October 2026 nights are still bookable (read 2026-10-12). --Claude

name: Tumbling Creek Campground
note: Primitive 8-site FCFS campground along Tumbling Creek near Ocoee #3 Lake, Cherokee NF (Ocoee/Big Frog Mountain region). No reservations (not on recreation.gov). Mostly small RVs/vans/cars, but the first couple of sites fit medium RVs/trailers with room to turn around (23-ft feasible). No designated pads, no hookups, no toilets/water/tables; max 5 people per site; bear-proof food storage required. Access via gravel FR 45/FR 221; easiest approach is paved Grassy Creek Rd off Hwy 68 then ~2 mi on FR 221 — passable by a normal vehicle. Open year-round. FCFS — not on recreation.gov. --Claude

name: Big Oak Cove Campground
note: USFS Cherokee NF, Tellico Plains Ranger District. ~11-12 small primitive sites (gravel pads) on the Tellico River along paved Tellico River Rd (FR210). Picnic table, fire ring, lantern post, vault toilets; NO potable water, NO hookups. RV + tent (small rigs; sibling sites on this road fit ~25-26 ft). FCFS only -- no reservations on recreation.gov; pay on-site via Scan & Pay QR, ~$10/night. Seasonal, roughly mid-spring to fall (2025 open date May 22). Currently operating per 2025/26 USFS schedule. --Claude

name: North River Campground
note: Small (11-site) primitive Cherokee NF campground along North River, ~3 mi up gravel FR 217 off FR 210 from Tellico Plains. Drive-in; FS notes 'Sites 2 and 3 are ideal for mid-sized campers and trailers' and sites 4-6 for mid/smaller rigs (firsthand report of a 25-ft truck camper; low branches a caveat for tall rigs). Vault toilets, no potable water; bear food storage. FCFS only, open year-round. Operated by Cherokee National Forest (Tellico River Ranger District). --Claude

name: Look Rock Campground
note: GSMNP campground (reopened); 68 sites incl 10 with electric+water hookups (30/50-amp) -- the first Smokies campground to offer hookups -- plus dump station; remaining 58 sites no hookups. No showers. Reservation-required online only, no FCFS. Seasonal (~May-late Oct). Bear food-storage rules enforced. --Claude

name: Paint Creek
note: Cherokee NF campground along Paint Creek; 20 sites (sites 13/14/16 tent-only -> 17 RV-capable), pads ~50x25 ft so a 23-ft rig fits. No hookups; vault toilets. FCFS scan-and-pay (not advance-reservable). Narrow/steep access road -- fine for 23 ft, not big rigs. Season ~May 5-Oct 24. --Claude

name: Boswell Landing
note: LBL NRA self-service campground (USFS) on the Tennessee side near Dover; ~16-19 primitive sites, gravel pads, paved 5-mi access road. No hookups; vault toilets, fire rings, dumpster, boat ramp. FCFS - pay by fee envelope at the iron ranger (not on recreation.gov). Open year-round, 14-day max. --Claude

name: Gatlin Point
note: LBL NRA self-service campground (USFS) at the south end on a Lake Barkley embayment near Dover; ~18-19 primitive sites, gravel pads, gravel-road access. No hookups (drinking water in campground, none at sites); vault toilets, dumpster, boat ramp. FCFS - fee envelope at the iron ranger (not on recreation.gov). Note: first entrance is steep and some aprons sit at an awkward angle for trailers. --Claude

name: Winchester Parks and Recreation Campground
note: City of Winchester municipal campground next to Tims Ford Lake and the community ball fields (1895 Phillip Fulmer Pkwy). 28 sites with 20/30/50-amp electric and water, some full-hookup; tents OK. Seasonal Apr 1-Oct 31. Reservable by phone or city website. RV Life: 1.5* / $ (thin reviews, public park). --Claude

name: Wiseman Park
note: Metro Lynchburg/Moore County municipal campground - a paved-and-grass lot behind the downtown square, a short walk from the Jack Daniel's Distillery. ~20 sites: a handful of 50/30-amp full-hookup spots plus several 15-amp sites; water at select sites; ~40-ft max. FCFS, pay at the courthouse (walking distance) or by mail. Access runs through the town square - tight during festivals but passable for a 23-ft rig. Currently operating. --Claude

name: Bradley's Pit BBQ & Grill RV Sites
note: Restaurant in Sweetwater with 6 level gravel RV sites (30/50A; 2 with water), $20/night, room for RVs/buses/semis. Also a Harvest Hosts location. Small but a real drive-in nightly RV stop. RV Life 4.5★/$$, 3 reviews; specifics confirmed on operator page. --Claude

name: Brooks Corner Campground & RV Park
note: Behind R.M. Brooks Store near historic Rugby; 10 full-service sites (7x30A/3x50A), bathhouse, WiFi, reservations accepted. Adjacent to a Big South Fork trailhead, ~1 mi from Clear Fork River. RV Life 5★/$$, 2 reviews; specifics confirmed on operator listing. --Claude

name: Buchanan Resort
note: Kentucky Lake fishing/RV resort est. 1946, Springville; open mid-March–mid-Nov. Three campgrounds with gravel full/partial-hookup sites for RVs up to 40 ft; nightly/monthly/seasonal. 350-slip marina, restaurant, store, pool. RV Life 4★/$$, 3 reviews; nightly camping confirmed on operator site. --Claude

name: Coops Creek RV Campground
note: Small private 10-slip full-hookup RV park (W/S/E, 30/50A, WiFi) in downtown Dunlap, adjacent to Coke Ovens Historical Park with a foot path to Coops Creek. Reserve by phone/email. Operating per Dunlap Mercantile listing and active FB page. RV Life 5★/$$, 2 reviews (thin). --Claude

name: Crazy Horse Recreational Park
note: The original Buffalo River outfitter, family-run for 35 years at Bell Bridge on Hwy 13 just north of Waynesboro. Its North and South campgrounds have 30/50-amp electric-and-water RV sites along over a mile of river frontage (a few septic sites for monthly stays), free showers and restrooms, a camp store, and canoe and kayak floats. Open April to October. First come, first served with no reservations; cash only, paid at the gate or to a camping assistant; the gates are never locked; no generators. Office and South Campground at 2505 Waynesboro Hwy, North Campground at 2501. --Claude

Fees: +$10/night each adult over 2, children 12 and under free

name: Green Acres
note: Small private RV park at 6403 S York Hwy, Clarkrange; 21 full-hookup sites (water, 30/50A electric, sewer), backs to a working cattle farm with on-site coffee shop. Nightly/weekly/monthly; reservable via own site or phone. No on-site water. RV Life 5★/$$, 1 review (confirmed operating). --Claude

name: Hatchie Cove Campground
note: Small family-run private RV park at 2553 Marvin Chapel Rd, Brownsville, off I-40; full hookups (50A, W, S), fits up to a 36-ft Class A per reviews. Open year-round; reservations required (booked via parkwith.us). RV Life 4.5★/$$, 48 reviews. Name refers to the nearby Hatchie River area, not on-site water. --Claude

name: McMillan Farms
note: Private farm retreat at 495 McMillan Rd, Mosheim; general campground (offers horse/hiking trails, not equestrian-only) with 7 full-hookup back-in sites for RVs of any size, bathhouse, on-site fishing ponds. Gated, reservation required (email/phone). RV Life 4.5★/$$, 9 reviews; confirmed operating. --Claude

name: Mountain Pass Campground
note: Private RV campground on the Powell River near Cumberland Gap, 575 Benfield Lane, Harrogate. ~56 gravel full-hookup sites (30/50A), big-rig pull-throughs; daily rental or yearly lease. Reservable by phone/email. River access, boat launch. RV Life 4★/$$, 13 reviews; operating per Campendium. --Claude

name: Old Mountain Campground
note: Family-run private campground at base of Viking Mtn, 1074 Old Mountain Rd, Greeneville. ~26 RV sites (8x 50A, 18x 30A) full hookups, pool, offers horse trails (general CG, not equestrian-only); open year-round, FCFS/by phone. Confirmed operating via operator site. --Claude

name: Outer Haven Campground
note: Family-run private campground, 4111 Chavis Rd, Cosby, ~6 mi from GSMNP Cosby entrance. 17 graveled RV sites (1-10 full hookup, 11-17 W/E); site pads 55-75 ft long, fit a 23-ft rig easily. Booked nightly via Airbnb; operating. RV Life 4★/$$, 1 review; tent + glamping also on-site. --Claude

name: Swiss Haven RV Campground
note: Small private full-hookup RV park near Hohenwald (300 Gay Rd); 16 sites, 50-amp (5 also 20/30-amp), 3 pull-throughs. Official site, currently operating; reservations by phone while booking engine upgraded. Thinly reviewed (RV Life 4★/$$, 4 reviews) but operator page confirms a transient nightly RV park. --Claude

name: High Falls State Park Lakeside Campground
note: The smaller of High Falls State Park's two camping areas: a wooded loop on its own entrance road north of High Falls Road, set back from 650-acre High Falls Lake behind the park's six yurts, with a campers-only dock on the lake. The River Campground, 1.4 km south below the falls, is a separate entry. The park posted (read 2026-10-29) that High Falls Lake will be lowered between November 1, 2026 and January 31, 2027. --Claude

name: Tallulah Gorge State Park Campground
note: Terrora campground. Sandy beach on Tallulah Falls Lake at the adjacent Terrora day-use area; the park page says the beach is closed for construction (swimming area and an ADA kayak launch), with kayaking unavailable until the work is done (read 2026-10-30). --Claude

name: Vogel State Park
note: Mountainous terrain — not for large RVs. 22-acre Lake Trahlyta is drained for dam repairs, with the lake loop trail and the waterfall closed; campsites remain open (park page, read 2026-10-29). --Claude

name: Lake Winfield Scott Campground
note: USFS Chattahoochee NF (Blue Ridge RD), run by concessionaire FIND Outdoors; on 18-acre Lake Winfield Scott near Suches (electric motors only, swimming beach). South Loop holds the hookup and longer sites; North Loop stays open in winter. CLOSED from Sep 1, 2026 for construction and renovation, no reopening date (checked 2026-10-30). --Claude

name: Ruth B. Kirby Gilchrist Blue Springs State Park
note: Distinct from Orange City's Blue Spring SP. Since Oct 29, 2025 there are no water activities (spring closed for construction renovations; portable toilets in place until they are complete); camping still sold on Reserve Florida (read 2026-10-21). --Claude

name: Myakka River State Park
note: Big Flats campground sits near the Upper Myakka Lake, the Myakka Outpost and Wi-Fi; Old Prairie and Palmetto Ridge are near the SR 72 entrance and the river, and only Palmetto Ridge has sewer. Drinking water has been unavailable park-wide since Oct. 28, 2025 - bring your own; bottled water is free at the ranger station (park page, read 2026-10-21). --Claude

name: Saddle Creek Park Campground
note: Polk County campground at 750-acre Saddle Creek Park, Lakeland; loop in an oak hammock near the back of the park among former-phosphate-pit lakes. Reopened Oct 2024 after hurricane closures. The low RV Life rating reflects dated reviews of an aging bathhouse, not a closure. No campfires at Saddle Creek; after-hours entry must be pre-scheduled with the resident park caretaker (Polk County rules, read 2026-10-21). --Claude

name: Lake Fisher Park
note: Six E/W sites w/table and fire pit, close to a 100-acre fishing lake.  FCFS, self register.

name: Brushy Lake Campground
note: Small Bankhead NF campground on Brushy Lake; no hookups, FCFS. --Claude

name: Pine Glen Recreation Area
note: Talladega NF campground on Shoal Creek; no hookups, FCFS. --Claude

name: Turnipseed Campground
note: Small Talladega NF campground off the Talladega Scenic Drive; no hookups, FCFS. FS lists it as an RV-usable developed campground. --Claude

name: Cherokee Rock Village
note: Cherokee County park atop Lookout Mountain (Sand Rock); 15 primitive RV-accessible sites (rigs to 40 ft), no hookups but dump station, bathhouse and hot showers. Some sites reservable; tent area FCFS. --Claude

name: Wheeler Reservation Campground
note: Lauderdale County campground on Wheeler Lake (Tennessee River) near Wheeler Dam at Elgin (county-operated on TVA reservation land); 28 water/electric sites, bathhouse/showers, fishing pier, dump station. Seasonal; FCFS after opening weekend. --Claude

name: Archusa Creek Water Park
note: Pat Harrison Waterway District water park near Quitman; 69 sites (56 full-hookup, 13 electric/water), 30/50 amp, max RV ~38 ft, dump station, bathhouses. Reservable; also takes FCFS. Note: the reservoir was drained following a dam breach - confirm water status before relying on lakefront sites.

name: Lake Claude Bennett
note: MDWFP State Fishing Lake ~20 mi E of Bay Springs off Hwy 18 near Rose Hill (Jasper Co.); 71-acre lake. 31 RV sites with electric (50-amp) + water (no sewer) and dump station; also 4 rental cabins. Camping permit $360/30-day; FCFS — call the state lake office, no online reservations. Boat ramp, fishing for bass, bream, crappie. RV Life: unrated (0★), $.

name: Lake Columbia
note: MDWFP State Fishing Lake ~7 mi SE of Columbia (Marion Co./Foxworth); 84-acre lake. ~6-12 paved RV back-in sites with electric (30-amp) + water, dump station, handicap accessible, plus tent sites; bathhouse with showers, boat ramps, fishing piers. FCFS — call the state lake office, no online reservations. RV Life: unrated (0★), $.

name: Lake Jeff Davis
note: MDWFP State Fishing Lake just outside Prentiss (Jefferson Davis Co.); 100-acre lake. 13 paved back-in RV sites with electric (30-amp) + water + picnic tables, dump station, plus 10 tent sites; 3 handicap-access fishing piers, double boat ramp (ramp fee $7/boat). FCFS — call the state lake office, no online reservations. Open year-round.

name: Lake Lamar Bruce
note: MDWFP State Fishing Lake ~1.5 mi NE of Saltillo off US-45 (Lee Co.); 300-acre lake — the only public water in MS stocked with rainbow trout. 11 sites with water + electric plus primitive camping; concrete boat ramp with courtesy piers, 5 handicap-access fishing piers, pavilion, restrooms/showers. FCFS — call the state lake office, no online reservations.
